```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Layered tissues (cortex, epidermis, airway wall) are organised along a depth
axis. If spots or cells are grouped into ordered depth windows, for example
from a GASTON isodepth or from annotated layers, LongOmicsTraj can treat the
windows as visits, tissue sections as subjects and donors or disease groups
as groups. This vignette shows the workflow on simulated pseudobulk data.

## Simulated pseudobulk

Three donors with four sections each; three windows (upper, deep, white
matter). Two kinds of window-wide shift are built in:

* a biological shift shared by all donors: 70% of genes fall from the deep
  window into white matter;
* a technical offset in donor 2 only: every gene is raised in the deep and
  white-matter windows (capture efficiency or composition differs).

```{r simulate}
library(LongOmicsTraj)
set.seed(1)
G <- 300; visits <- c("upper", "deep", "WM")
truth <- matrix(sample(c(-1, 0, 1), 2 * G, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.2, 0.6, 0.2)), G)
base <- rnorm(G, 2)
falls <- runif(G) < 0.7
truth[falls, 2] <- -1
prof <- cbind(base, base + 0.5 * truth[, 1], base + 0.5 * truth[, 1] + 0.5 * truth[, 2])
truth_label <- paste(c("down", "flat", "up")[truth[, 1] + 2], c("down", "flat", "up")[truth[, 2] + 2], sep = "_")
meta <- expand.grid(window = visits, section = 1:4, donor = 1:3, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
E <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(meta)), function(i) {
  w <- match(meta$window[i], visits)
  prof[, w] + rnorm(G, 0, 0.15) + if (meta$donor[i] == 2 && w > 1) 0.4 else 0
})
rownames(E) <- paste0("gene", seq_len(G))
md <- data.frame(
  sample_id  = paste0("d", meta$donor, "_s", meta$section, "_", meta$window),
  subject_id = paste0("d", meta$donor, "_s", meta$section),
  visit      = meta$window,
  group      = paste0("Donor", meta$donor)
)
colnames(E) <- md$sample_id
```

## Workflow

`lot_compute_deltas()` offers three ways to handle window-wide shifts:

* `center = "none"` keeps them;
* `center = "median"` removes every window-wide shift, technical or biological;
* `center = "relative"` removes only each group's deviation from the shift
  shared by all groups, so shared biology is kept and group-specific offsets
  are removed.

We compare the three by accuracy against the simulated truth and by
agreement across donors.

```{r workflow}
run <- function(center) {
  l <- lot_create(expression = E, metadata = md, assay = "rna", visit_levels = visits,
                  time_values = c(upper = 1, deep = 2, WM = 3), feature_type = "gene")
  l <- lot_from_empirical(l, assay = "rna", visits = visits, group_col = "group",
                          visit_col = "visit", estimator = "empirical", verbose = FALSE)
  l <- lot_compute_deltas(l, assay = "rna", visits = visits, center = center)
  l <- lot_compute_thresholds(l, assay = "rna", visits = visits, method = "hybrid",
                              verbose = FALSE)
  lot_map_to_ots(l, assay = "rna", visits = visits, verbose = FALSE)
}
score <- function(l) {
  o <- as.data.frame(l@ots)
  W <- reshape(o[, c("object_id", "group", "topology_label")], idvar = "object_id",
               timevar = "group", direction = "wide")
  W <- W[match(rownames(E), W$object_id), ]
  c(accuracy = mean(as.matrix(W[, -1]) == truth_label),
    agreement = mean(W[, 2] == W[, 3] & W[, 3] == W[, 4]))
}
sapply(c("none", "median", "relative"), function(cc) round(score(run(cc)), 2))
```

The shared shift and the offset removed from each donor are stored with the
results. Only donor 2 has a large offset, and the shared fall into white
matter is kept:

```{r offsets}
l <- run("relative")
as.data.frame(l@results$visit_centring)
```

## Choosing a centring option

Median centring assumes that, within each window transition, most genes do
not change, or change up and down in roughly equal numbers. When many genes
truly shift in one direction in every group, as here, it removes part of
that real signal and mislabels unchanged genes. Relative centring needs no
such assumption, but it needs at least three groups to estimate the shared
shift robustly. We recommend `"relative"` with three or more groups, and
inspecting `results$visit_centring` in every case.
